published_statement: Carroll gr-qc/9712019 p.81: 'R_{rho sigma mu nu} = -R_{sigma rho mu nu} allows us to write this result as nabla_[lambda R_rho sigma] mu nu = 0 . (3.88) This is known as the Bianchi identity. (Notice that for a general connection there would be additional terms involving the torsion tensor.) ... An especially useful form of the Bianchi identity comes from contracting twice on (3.87): 0 = g^{nu sigma} g^{mu lambda}(nabla_lambda R_{rho sigma mu nu} + nabla_rho R_{sigma lambda mu nu} + nabla_sigma R_{lambda rho mu nu}) = nabla^mu R_{rho mu} - nabla_rho R + nabla^nu R_{rho nu} , (3.93) or nabla^mu R_{rho mu} = (1/2) nabla_rho R . (3.94) (Notice that, unlike the partial derivative, it makes sense to raise an index on the covariant derivative, due to metric compatibility.) If we define the Einstein tensor as G_{mu nu} = R_{mu nu} - (1/2) R g_{mu nu} , (3.95) then we see that the twice-contracted Bianchi identity (3.94) is equivalent to nabla^mu G_{mu nu} = 0 . (3.96)'. p.117: 'In the absence of some constraints on T_{mu nu}, the answer is "any metric at all"; simply take the metric of your choice, compute the Einstein tensor G_{mu nu} for this metric, and then demand that T_{mu nu} be equal to G_{mu nu}. (It will automatically be conserved, by the Bianchi identity.)' p.118: T_{mu nu} = -Lambda g_{mu nu} 'is automatically conserved by metric compatibility'.
published_hypotheses: Christoffel (Levi-Civita) connection: torsion-free AND metric-compatible. Torsion: 'for a general connection there would be additional terms involving the torsion tensor' (p.81); metric compatibility: needed to raise the index through nabla in the contraction (p.81, note after 3.94); 'Our primary concern is with the Christoffel connection, for which (3.90) is the only independent contraction' and the Ricci tensor is symmetric (3.91).

the identity is DIFFERENTIAL: (3.88) is the second Bianchi identity (closely related to the Jacobi identity for [[nabla,nabla],nabla], eq. 3.89), not a consequence of the algebraic symmetries (3.64 etc.) alone
metric differentiable enough for nabla R to exist classically (third derivatives of g enter nabla G; C^3 is sufficient) -- implicit in the source
no field equation is assumed for (3.96) itself; the conservation consequence requires G_{mu nu} = 8 pi G T_{mu nu} (optionally with -Lambda g_{mu nu}, itself conserved by metric compatibility)

conservation obtained is LOCAL covariant conservation nabla_mu T^{mu nu} = 0 (4.23); Carroll p.37 separately notes that gravitational energy has no sensible local tensor, so this is not an integral energy law in general
any dimension (the contraction does not use n = 4)

The source derives it from the second (differential) Bianchi identity of the Christoffel connection, flags torsion terms for a general connection, and uses metric compatibility to contract. Computed here (rederive B1): phi(x)(g_ac g_bd - g_ad g_bc) on flat space carries EVERY algebraic Riemann symmetry, first Bianchi included, yet its contracted G = -3 phi eta has div G = -3 d phi != 0; (B2) a metric-compatible connection with torsion and a torsion-free non-metric connection each give nabla_mu G^{mu nu} != 0.
